plan.title: Some Lines Are Straighter Than Others
plan.blurb: Shot straight down from the air, each photograph is cut in two by the edge where land meets water, but each edge is drawn by a different hand. In Melbourne the line is ruled by man, a hard sea wall holding back the city; in Sardinia it is drawn by the sea against a rough edge of fallen rock; and at Wilsons Promontory it is barely a line at all, just water and sand dissolving into each other. Read together, the series moves from a threshold that is built to one that is negotiated and finally to one that is never fixed, redrawn by every wave. DJI Mavic Pro drone, all three images (edited in Adobe Lightroom)

plan.title: One Step Further
plan.blurb: Each gate marks one step further in, and then another. The path bends out of sight, so you keep walking to see what comes next. The threshold becomes the journey.
plan.subject: Fushimi Inari-taisha in Kyoto, Japan

plan.doc: C:\Users\RivinduB\Desktop\Submission\Serena Franco\2026 Photography Exhibition Written Submission Template_Serena Franco.docx
plan.title: No Rush
plan.blurb: The walls are bare, the floor is broken, and the light is somewhere ahead. He walks toward it without hurrying. It’s the moment between where you’ve been and where you’re going.
plan.subject: A man walking in an abandoned building in Naples, Italy

plan.title: The Last Line
plan.blurb: Surf on one side, sand on the other, and a thin strip of in-between where everyone seems to end up. Some walk it, some pause. Nobody is in a hurry to leave it.
plan.subject: A beach in Byron Bay

plan.title: Frame the Horizon
plan.blurb: The sea stays the same and only the way you see it changes. One steel loop is enough to turn open water into a destination. A frame can be a threshold too.
plan.subject: Sculpture by the Sea, Bondi Beach
